criteria: Actual queue/admission/routing population and server-occupancy boundary.
Poisson/renewal/IID/stationarity assumptions beyond first two moments.
Exact occupancy/mean results versus approximations and unsupported tail extrapolation.
Finite loss, waiting, discipline, abandonment and outcome accounting.

noChangeEvidence.observation: Existing workflow acquires selected boundary/topology and source/measurement evidence, permits narrow arithmetic or no change, and does not equate CV with distribution or endpoint response with service time.

Already preserves Erlang-B applicability to general IID holding times in a no-wait loss system, separates it from waiting formulas, and ties finite occupancy reductions to actual transition rates rather than discipline labels alone.
Already states queue-wait point mass/quantile scope and stable B-to-C computation with input/domain checks; does not use mean corrections to invent general-service tails.
Already follows actual executor capacity behavior and task lifecycle, labels submission delay accurately, preserves rejection/cancellation semantics and qualifies JFR/ThreadMXBean coverage.
Already preserves transient backlog reflection and delayed capacity, interprets residuals as competing hypotheses, and separates caller departure from actual work termination.

preserved: Model selection and falsification role; boundaries with Little's Law, pool sizing, USL and latency statistics.
M/M/1, M/M/c, M/G/1, M/D/1, GI/G/1 and Allen–Cunneen decision rules with exact/approximate/tail distinctions.
General-holding Erlang loss insensitivity with its prerequisites, finite capacity and discipline-sensitive class outcomes.
Shared versus routed/partition-affine queues, open/closed/semi-open population and retry feedback.
Service-position occupancy, multi-load parameter dependence, censoring, inventory reconciliation and cohort accounting.
Stable Erlang recursion and numeric domains, reflected fluid backlog and finite-loss accounting.
Partial Java 8+ lifecycle snippet and JDK 25 observation boundaries, without upgrade authorization.
Existing no-change/limited-result choices; no new campaigns, generic checklists or forced topology changes.
All five shipped files unchanged by SHA-256.

twoCases.prerequisites: Read queueing-models and routed model/topology references. The fixtures define an analytical design scenario, not a claim that production telemetry has already proved its assumptions. No Java or dependencies are required; optional deterministic arithmetic or a bounded temporary numerical experiment is allowed.

taskInput.task: Review the proposed Erlang-B calculation for the active configuration. Determine whether it can supply exact steady-state rejection probability and carried throughput here. Compute justified quantities or give the smallest suitable alternative and the remaining validation limit. Preserve the supplied workload and admission contract; do not silently substitute exponential holding times, add waiting slots or switch to an infinite queue.

files.decision.md: We are budgeting admission loss for two equivalent resource slots. The proposed worksheet uses Erlang B with the mean slot-holding time. Check the active configuration before approving that choice.
files.admission-contract.md: On arrival, a free resource slot starts the operation immediately. Otherwise an operation waits FCFS only when a configured waiting slot is available; if not, it is rejected. Holding time begins on acquisition and ends on release. A completed operation frees its slot and starts the oldest waiter immediately. There are no retries, timeout, cancellation, priorities, reservations, state-dependent admission or shared-resource slowdown. The holding-time law and arrival process in the configuration are stipulated inputs. State separately what applying the result to production would still require.
files.active-admission.yaml:
resource_slots: 2
waiting_slots: 0
discipline: FCFS
on_full: reject
retries: none
abandonment: none
arrivals:
  process: stationary_poisson
  rate_per_second: 2
holding_time:
  law: iid_two_point
  seconds: [0.5, 1.5]
  probabilities: [0.5, 0.5]
  independent_of_arrivals: true
  independent_of_occupancy: true

evaluatorExpectations.decisiveEvidence: No waiting places and immediate rejection at two occupied slots; stationary Poisson arrivals and IID independent holding times with mean one second.
evaluatorExpectations.acceptableOutcome: Retain Erlang B through the M/G/2/2 loss-system insensitivity property, despite non-exponential holding times. Offered load a=2 Erlangs; blocking=0.4; admitted/carried rate=1.2 per second. State the input assumptions and distinguish this model result from production validation.
observableCriteria: Uses the actual admission boundary and zero waiting slots.
Does not reject Erlang B solely because service is bimodal or offered rho equals one.
Does not apply Erlang-C queue-wait/tail formulas or use offered lambda unchanged as carried throughput.
failureConditions: Insists exponential service is required for this loss probability.
Treats rho=1 as absence of a stationary finite loss distribution.
Reports queue wait or a response percentile from Erlang B.
Claims the arithmetic validated the real workload assumptions.
